text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- State Comptroller won't probe Labour party leader Ehud Barak over Tseelim-2 army accident when he was army chief.
- Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai, Palestinian cabinet minister Nabil Shaath meet.
- Two Israeli border policemen injured by bomb near Nablus.
- Angry National Infrastructure Minister Ariel Sharon cuts short meeting with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
- New Finance Minister Yaacov Neeman: Central bank should move closer to Treasury's view.
- GM, Elbit to discuss joint R&D.
- Trade deficit down 22 percent to $4.3 billion.
- Members of Israel's Knesset, Generali agree on $12 million Holocaust fund.
GLOBES

- Yaacov Neeman enters finance ministry: "We'll not impose cuts on the public". He intends to present ideas to prime minister already on Sunday. "Bank of Israel sets monetary policy, but we will work together," Neeman said.
HAARETZ
- Neeman: "Budget will be cut by 600 million shekels. I will lower tax burden".
- Fear in Netanyahu's office: Sharon will prevent approval of diplomatic decisions.
MAARIV
- U.S. President Bill Clinton: Fear of deterioration in Middle East peacemaking; drafting programme for renewing negotiations.
- Reconciliation meeting of Sharon and Netanayhu blows up after only three minutes.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Bank of Israel will allow bank actions by way of Internet.
